item.description:
• Minutes in zone this week. Home and Progress show how many minutes you have ridden this week, Monday to Sunday, in Endurance (zones 2–3) and VO₂max (zones 5–6), as small batteries that fill towards a weekly target of your own. Set the targets in Settings (⌘,), where Anifora suggests your average of the last four weeks; Threshold (zone 4) can be switched on there too. Every ride you have saved counts already; demo rides never do.
  • …and during the ride. With a target set, small rings after the mode at the top left fill with the week's minutes, this ride's part bright. Click them for the whole week. A card comes for a few seconds when a zone starts counting, another tenth of a target fills or a target is reached. Switch both off in the ride menu (Esc) or in Settings.
  • Collect minutes in a ride. Click the rings, then Collect minutes this ride under a zone: choose the minutes (they start at what your week still misses, spread over the days left) and collect them on your gears, or press Hold it for me: ERG holds the middle of Z2 for Endurance or Z4 for Threshold (± moves it inside the zone), and VO₂max comes as 4-minute reps with 3 minutes easy between. A capsule beside the mode shows how far along you are; click it or the rings to change or stop the goal. When the minutes are in, a card says so and the ride goes back to your gears.
  • What fills your week. Each workout in the library says how many of your week's missing minutes it would fill, zone by zone, and the order Fills my week puts the best fits first. Home names the one that fills most, with a Load button.
  • Try it on the demo trainer. A demo ride has a demo week of its own, with its own targets, so the rings, the cards and Collect can all be tried without real riding. It is never saved and never counts towards your own week.

• The power bar shows your zone. Only the zone you are in lights up, with a pin at your watts. Drag the pin and the trainer holds those watts in ERG instead of your gears; the gear panel turns into the watts held, with ± and Back to gears (or press G). On a climb you hold in a zone, the pin fine-tunes that climb's watts.
  • How you sit moved to the ride menu (Esc) in 3D, and stays on ↑ ↓. The gear panel is smaller.
  • The top left says ERG while a climb is held in a zone — it used to show the road's own number.
  • A quieter ride screen in 3D. Lap, Pause and Stop no longer sit at the top of the road for the whole ride. Press Esc, or Menu at the top right, for the ride menu: Pause, Lap and End ride, how the climb is ridden, the intensity, power match, Devices, Leave 3D and the other pages. The ride carries on while the menu is open. Space pauses and resumes, and End ride asks once more before it ends the ride.
  • A smaller Start. Before the ride, one small bar above the profile shows what is ready (rider, trainer, heart rate) next to the Start button. Until a trainer is connected the button reads Connect trainer and opens Devices; once it is connected it turns green, and Return starts.

• An intro before hill repeats. Press Start on a hill repeat and the camera first circles the climb once, the whole of it in view, with one card beside it: the climb, the power to hold, how long each time up and each rest take you, and the whole session. Then it comes down to you and the ride begins right there, with the panels fading back in. Ride, Esc or Space start the ride at once. Press I any time, on the start line or during the ride, to watch it again.
  • Hold a climb in a zone. On a road, the climb card that comes up a minute before each climb now has five small buttons, Z1 to Z5, each with its watts. Pick one (or press 1–5) and the trainer holds that power from the foot to the top, whatever gear you are in. At the top the ride goes back to how you were riding. Zones you could not hold to the top are greyed out, worked out from your own threshold and reserve; hover over one to see why. If your reserve runs out or you stop pedalling, the climb is let go and the card says so. Press the same button again, or 0, to let it go yourself.
  • Auto shift keeps up at the foot of a climb. Coming off a descent in a big gear, auto shift now makes one big shift straight to the gear for the climb ahead, like dropping to the small chainring, instead of one gear every two seconds. It also no longer holds a hard gear because your power fell under its floor while your cadence was collapsing.
